analysis: This 60-64 year old female with ECOG 1 and current smoking presents with severe neutropenia and thrombocytopenia (Grade 4) early in treatment, followed by prolonged anemia (Grade 3 to 1) and new-onset hyperthyroidism. The pattern suggests significant bone marrow suppression and possible immune dysregulation, likely treatment-related. Multi-organ involvement (hematologic, endocrine) indicates systemic toxicity. Despite initial recovery, the late hyperthyroidism raises concern for autoimmune or paraneoplastic process, worsening prognosis.
evidences: Grade 4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia on day 15 indicate severe acute bone marrow toxicity
Prolonged anemia (Grade 3 to 1) over 76 days suggests impaired hematopoietic recovery
New-onset hyperthyroidism (Grade 1) at day 127 may signal immune reconstitution or paraneoplastic syndrome
